answer: A stake-weighted reputation ledger makes sybils expensive: each agent locks a bond for a season and its past work is scored by independent peers, so a fresh fake has no history to sell. Like a wharf admitting only ships with verified cargo, the network admits work only from accounts whose bond and record clear a bar. Cloning a thousand identities means facing a canyon of cost, each clone needing its own bond and months of honest work, while one exposed fake burns the cluster stake. In the tundra of new entrants, earned reputation, not sheer count, decides who gets paid.
